rows.capability: Live multi-person room with a separate mix-minus for each person

weavesignal.note: Presenters, guests and callers join a WebRTC room (LiveKit); the desk gives each person a mix of the show without their own voice. A two-person conversation over two real networks is not yet proved by ear (one-person run only).

others.note: Its Web DJ lets one DJ broadcast from a browser; no multi-guest room is described.

Several guests in one session who hear one another; Cleanfeed's blog says mix-minus is handled for guests. Reported, not read on a product page. Hosted, not on your server.

Group rooms with a director; its docs describe monitor mixes and excluding the director's audio, not a per-person programme return.
Broadcast phone hybrid system with mix-minus into the console (Livewire); callers by SIP, not a browser.

choose_other_if.when: You mainly play music or pre-recorded shows, want one web admin for several stations, or want years of community knowledge. Add Cleanfeed or a similar tool for guests.
You are moving from Airtime or want an AM/FM-style scheduling and library tool with AGPL licensing.
You run a broadcast studio on Linux with touchscreen live assist, voicetracking and traffic-system integration, and feed an encoder separately.
You do not want to run a server. Live365 also sells music licensing cover for the USA, Canada and Mexico; check what your plan includes.
You only need a guest link with very good audio and a simple interface, and you already have a way to stream.
You want remote guests into a DAW or OBS and a studio mixer, and you do not need a call-in page or a screener.

choose_other_if.tool: Telos VX or another phone hybrid
choose_other_if.when: Callers must ring a real telephone number, or your studio already runs a broadcast console and a PBX.
You want total control, have an engineer, and will write and maintain the scripts yourself.
Your community already lives there; WeaveSignal's chat is separate, with its own login and moderation.
